---
title: "Output visualization"
---

The iLand Viewer provides a built-in Output visualization tab alongside the spatial Landscape view. It visualizes SQLite [output tables](outputs.qmd) directly during a simulation run, updating automatically every simulated year when the tab is active, and also lets you open and inspect finished `.sqlite` output databases without running a simulation.

## Overview

The central view of the [iLand Viewer](iland-viewer.qmd) is organized into two tabs, with linked side panels that switch automatically with the active tab.

The Landscape tab provides the interactive 2D visualization of trees, light fields, regeneration, disturbance grids, and resource units during a model run, paired with the Legend (left dock) and Visualization options (right dock).

The Output visualization tab provides a full-width canvas for time-series charts, monthly boxplots, and resource-unit spatial maps queried directly from the active SQLite output database. Its left dock (Output legend) displays either an interactive series/species legend—where items can be checked or unchecked to show or hide individual chart series—or a continuous/categorical color legend for spatial maps. Its right dock (Output options) contains the database source controls ("Open DB...", "Live"), the visualization catalog tree and search filter, selectors for the active metric, species, resource unit, color palette, and scale, and export actions ("Reset zoom", "Copy image", "Copy CSV").

### Data sources

Once a simulation model is created (`Model -> Create`), the tab connects to the active output database and refreshes automatically at the end of every simulated year whenever Output visualization is visible. Switching from Landscape back to Output visualization triggers an immediate catch-up refresh.

To inspect an existing iLand `.sqlite` output file without running a simulation, click "Open DB..." in the Output options dock to open the database in read-only mode. Click "Live" to switch back to a currently loaded simulation.

### Available plot types

Stacked area and line timelines cover species shares (colored with iLand species colors, with an optional "Normalize to 100%" toggle), carbon and nitrogen pools, annual and cumulative carbon fluxes, water balance, climate and permafrost variables, ABE planning unit harvests, and BITE agent summaries.

Bar and stacked bar timelines visualize sparse event tables such as `fire`, `wind`, `landscape_removed`, and `abeStandRemoval`, automatically zero-filling event-free years.

Monthly boxplots show seasonal distributions (`min`, `Q25`, `median`, `Q75`, `max`) across months 1–12 for `production_month` 3PG environmental modifiers.

#### Spatial maps (RU)

Interactive 2D resource-unit maps display simulation snapshots across years for the Dominant species map (`stand`) as well as continuous maps for `stand`, `sapling`, `carbon`, `carbonflow`, `water`, `standdead`, and `management`.

The Dominant species map determines the species with the highest share per resource unit (defaulting to basal area, or switchable to volume, stem count, LAI, living carbon, or NPP). Cells are colored by species color and given a dashed fill where the dominant species share is `< 50%`, matching iLand's classic Landscape view while supporting historical year scrubbing and external `.sqlite` files.

A Year slider above the map steps or jumps directly to any year snapshot present in the database, including decadal `conditionRU` intervals. For species-resolved continuous maps (`stand`, `sapling`, `standdead`, `management`), the Species selector offers `<Total (all species)>` and individual species. The Scale control switches between `Auto (year)` (rescaled per snapshot), `Auto 98% (year)` (clips the top 2% outlier cells so low- and mid-range patterns stay visible), `Global (all years)` (fixed range across all simulated years), and `Manual` (`Min`/`Max` range spinboxes).

When viewing a standalone `.sqlite` file ("Open DB..."), iLand automatically locates the project XML to reconstruct the resource-unit grid. Alternatively, click "Spatial grid..." in Output options to select a project XML or ASCII/GeoTIFF raster manually (this button is hidden in live simulation mode, where the model supplies the grid automatically).

## Customizing visualizations (`visualizations.json`)

The visualization catalog is defined in JSONC (JSON with `//` line comments and `/* ... */` block comments). You can customize existing entries or add visualizations for [dynamic / custom outputs](dynamic-outputs.qmd) without recompiling iLand.

### File lookup & override priority

Definitions are merged in three tiers by matching `"id"`:

1. Built-in defaults compiled into iLand (`:/visualizations.json`).
2. Global user file: `visualizations.json` placed in the iLand executable directory (applies to all projects).
3. Project user file: `visualizations.json` placed next to the active project XML file (or in `system.path.home`).

Click "Reload" in the Output options dock after saving edits to reload tiers 2 and 3 immediately. Click "?" next to "Reload" to view or export the built-in guide inside the Viewer.

To hide a built-in visualization, override its `"id"` with `"enabled": false`:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "visualizations": [
    { "id": "nitrogen_pools_landscape", "enabled": false }
  ]
}
```

### Field reference

Every `visualizations.json` file contains `"version": 1` and a `"visualizations"` array of definition objects:

| Key | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `id` | string | Required unique identifier. Matching an existing `id` overrides it. |
| `name` | string | Display name shown in the catalog, legend, and chart title. |
| `category` | string | Grouping header in the Output options catalog tree (default `"Custom"`). |
| `description` | string | Short description shown below the plot and as tooltip. |
| `table` | string | Primary SQLite table name (used by *Active outputs only* filtering). Leave empty for multi-table JOINs. |
| `type` | string | `"line"`, `"stacked_area"`, `"bar"`, `"stacked_bar"`, `"boxplot"`, or `"spatial"`. |
| `enabled` | boolean | Default `true`. Set `false` to hide an overridden built-in entry. |
| `sql` | string / string[] | SQLite `SELECT` query (a string array is joined with newlines). |
| `x` | string | X-axis column name (default `"year"`). |
| `xLabel` / `yLabel` | string | Optional axis labels. |
| `xCategories` | string[] | Optional category labels (e.g. `["Jan","Feb",...,"Dec"]` for `month` `1..12`). |
| `group` | string | Grouping column splitting rows into multiple series (e.g. `"species"`, `"reason"`). |
| `colorMode` | string | `"species"` uses species colors from the species table/model (auto-enabled when `group == "species"`). |
| `groupLabels` / `groupColors` | object | Optional maps from group codes to display labels or hex colors (`"#rrggbb"`). |
| `metricsMode` | string | `"select"` (dropdown, default) or `"all"` (plots all listed `metrics` together). |
| `metrics` | array | Objects `{ "col": "...", "label": "...", "color": "#...", "agg": "sum"|"none" }`. |
| `filters` | string[] | Filter dropdowns bound as `:name` in SQL (e.g. `["ru"]`, `["species", "ru"]`, `["id"]`, `["agent"]`). |
| `allowPercentToggle` | boolean | Enables the "Normalize to 100%" checkbox on stacked charts. |
| `fillMissingYears` | boolean | Zero-fills missing integer years (for sparse event tables). |
| `spatialKey` | string | For `"spatial"`: `"rid"` (environment ID, default) or `"ru"` (0-based RU index). |
| `palette` | string | For `"spatial"`: `"turbo"`, `"greens"`, `"rainbow"`, `"blues"`, `"reds"`, `"heat"`, or `"gray"`. |
| `speciesMode` | string | For `"spatial"`: `""`, `"select"`, `"select_with_aggregates"`, or `"dominant"`. |

### Named SQL parameters

Filter columns listed in `"filters"` are bound automatically as SQLite named parameters (`:ru`, `:species`, `:id`, `:agent`, `:reason`) and can be referenced directly in your SQL `WHERE` clause (e.g. `WHERE ru = :ru AND species = :species`). If a listed filter parameter is omitted from `sql`, iLand automatically wraps the query as `SELECT * FROM (<sql>) WHERE <filter> = :<filter>`. When `"filters"` includes `"ru"` and the table only contains landscape aggregate rows (`ru = -1`), iLand hides the RU dropdown automatically.

### Examples

#### Custom `dynamicstand` output

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "visualizations": [
    {
      "id": "custom_dynamicstand_dbh",
      "name": "Stand diameter distribution (dynamic)",
      "category": "Custom project charts",
      "description": "Mean and 90th-percentile DBH per species on a selected RU.",
      "table": "dynamicstand",
      "type": "line",
      "x": "year",
      "xLabel": "Year",
      "group": "species",
      "colorMode": "species",
      "filters": ["ru"],
      "metricsMode": "select",
      "metrics": [
        { "col": "dbh_mean",   "label": "Mean DBH (cm)" },
        { "col": "dbh_p90",    "label": "90th percentile DBH (cm)" },
        { "col": "volume_sum", "label": "Volume sum (m³)" }
      ],
      "sql": "SELECT year, species, dbh_mean, dbh_p90, volume_sum FROM dynamicstand WHERE ru = :ru ORDER BY year, species"
    }
  ]
}
```

#### Custom spatial map (`svdindicator`)

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "visualizations": [
    {
      "id": "custom_svd_shannon_map",
      "name": "Shannon diversity & IBP map",
      "category": "Spatial maps (RU)",
      "description": "Spatial map of SVD biodiversity and structural indicators.",
      "table": "svdindicator",
      "type": "spatial",
      "spatialKey": "rid",
      "palette": "turbo",
      "metricsMode": "select",
      "metrics": [
        { "col": "shannonIndex",      "label": "Shannon index" },
        { "col": "IBP",               "label": "Index of biodiversity potential" },
        { "col": "abovegroundCarbon", "label": "Aboveground C (t C/ha)" }
      ],
      "sql": "SELECT year, ru, rid, shannonIndex, IBP, abovegroundCarbon FROM svdindicator"
    }
  ]
}
```
